answer: A hollow defense lets one operator mint many islands of fake identity at no cost. Require instead a ferrous chain of sequential work: each identity must continuously evaluate a verifiable delay function seeded by its own key, advancing one step at a time. The chain cannot be parallelized or shared, so a single processor sustains only one live identity; every extra Sybil demands another processor running in real time, making the attacker's cost grow linearly with each fake identity.
